column2: **Jump search on sorted array of n=10000 elements uses block size m. Algorithm jumps m elements at a time, then linear searches within block. What block size minimizes comparisons?**
column3: Jump search: make n/m jumps, then linear search up to m elements in final block. Total comparisons ≈ n/m + m. Minimized when n/m = m, so m = √n. For n=10000, optimal m=100. Proof: derivative of (n/m + m) with respect to m equals zero at m=√n. Time complexity O(√n) with optimal block size.

**Lomuto partition scheme for QuickSort:**

```python
def lomuto_partition(arr, low, high):
    pivot = arr[high]
    i = low - 1
    
    for j in range(low, high):
        if arr[j] <= pivot:
            i += 1
            arr[i], arr[j] = arr[j], arr[i]
    
    arr[i + 1], arr[high] = arr[high], arr[i + 1]
    return i + 1
```

**Why is this partition scheme unstable?**
column3: Long-distance swaps in partition don't preserve relative order of equal elements. When arr[j] <= pivot, swapping arr[i] and arr[j] may separate equal elements that were adjacent. Hoare partition also unstable. Making QuickSort stable requires extra space to track original positions or using stable partition (less efficient).
